Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (VP of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s results for the Q2 FY2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s performance for the Q2 FY2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering robust top-line growth, expanding our backlog, and advancing our leadership in automation and digital solutions amid a complex global macro environment. North America continues to shine as our growth engine, with strong demand from reshoring trends in semiconductors and automotive, while our diversified footprint across regions has helped navigate headwinds elsewhere. We've also seen outstanding momentum in our automation and digital offerings, which are not only driving revenue but transforming efficiency for our customers and ourselves.

Let me dive deeper into one of our brightest growth stories this quarter: the explosive expansion of our Automation and Digital Offerings segment and its transformative impact on operational efficiency across our customers' factories. We're at the forefront of Industry 4.0 in the manufacturing and industrial equipment space, bridging the gap between traditional mechanical systems and smart, connected ecosystems. Our Automation and Digital segment delivered a stellar 28% year-over-year revenue growth, reaching $620 million—up from $485 million last year and now representing 32% of our total revenue, compared to just 25% a year ago. Within that, core automation hardware—like our next-gen Programmable Logic Controllers and servo drives—grew 22% to $380 million, fueled by demand for high-precision motion control in automotive and semiconductor fabs. But the real standout was our digital offerings, which surged 42% to $240 million. This includes our cloud-based IIoT platforms, AI-driven analytics suites, and subscription-based services, which now account for 45% of segment revenue—a jump from 35% last year. Recurring annual contract value from these digital services hit $180 million, up 55% year-over-year, with net retention rates holding steady at 118%, thanks to upsell opportunities in predictive maintenance and digital twins.

This isn't just top-line growth; it's profoundly reshaping efficiency for our customers and our own P&L. Segment-adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 420 basis points to 29.5%, driven by a software-like gross margin profile in our digital stack—now averaging 78%, versus 42% for hardware. On the customer side, we're delivering measurable ROI. For instance, our ApexEdge platform, which integrates edge computing with machine learning for real-time optimization, has boosted clients' Overall Equipment Effectiveness by an average of 17% across 450+ deployments. Take our partnership with a leading EV battery producer in the U.S. Midwest: Post-implementation of our predictive analytics module, they've cut unplanned downtime by 24%, from 8% to 6% of scheduled runtime, translating to $12 million in annual savings per plant. That's validated through our joint KPIs and third-party audits.

Technically, we're leaning into three key initiatives that are scaling rapidly. First, advanced IIoT and Edge AI: Our ApexEdge 2.0 processes 5x more data at the edge than competitors, reducing latency to under 10ms for closed-loop control in high-speed assembly lines. We've shipped 15,000 nodes year-to-date, with 60% in servo-robotics applications with native 5G connectivity for brownfield retrofits. Second, digital twins and simulation: Building on our SimForge acquisition, we've rolled out twin-enabled engineering services simulating entire production lines with 98% fidelity, shortening commissioning times by 35% and seeing strong uptake in aerospace for turbine assembly optimization. Third, cyber-resilient automation suites: Our SecurePAC platform embeds zero-trust architecture into PLCs, compliant with IEC 62443 standards, contributing 15% of automation bookings amid rising OT cybersecurity threats.

Regionally, North America drove 45% of segment growth at 35% year-over-year, fueled by reshoring and the CHIPS Act, with $150 million in orders from semiconductor expansions. Europe grew 18%, with efficiency plays aiding EU Green Deal mandates. Asia-Pacific hit 22% growth, led by Japan and South Korea's robotics boom, while we pivot to India for textile automation. We're investing $250 million in FY24 R&D, up 20% year-over-year, focusing on generative AI for anomaly detection, targeting a 25% reduction in mean-time-to-repair by year-end. Partnerships like our co-development with NVIDIA on GPU-accelerated edge AI position us for 25-30% segment compounding through 2025, driving 300-400 basis points of incremental group margin expansion.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives, including these digital advancements, are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—and thank you for joining us on the Q2 FY2024 earnings call for Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. Before I hand it over for more strategic updates, let me dive into our revenue performance by geographic region, along with other key financial metrics. I'm pleased to report that total revenue for the quarter came in at $1.28 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially from Q1. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth, driven by robust demand for our core product lines, including CNC machining centers, robotic automation systems, and precision forging equipment. I'll start with the top line in more detail. Total revenue came in at $1.28 billion, representing a strong increase year-over-year. Organic revenue growth was robust, driven primarily by higher volumes in our core machinery and automation segments, coupled with pricing realization across the board.

Our book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.25x, with a record backlog of $4.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year, signaling strong visibility into FY2025. Let me break this down by region, where we saw divergent trends reflecting both macroeconomic tailwinds and our targeted execution on reshoring, digital transformation, and sustainability initiatives. Geographically, North America accounted for 47% of revenue, or $602 million, up 25% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter. This was our standout performer, fueled by the continued U.S. manufacturing renaissance under the CHIPS Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. We've seen accelerated capex from OEMs in the automotive and aerospace sectors—think Boeing and Ford ramping up domestic supply chains for EV battery assembly lines and next-gen aircraft components. Our ThunderForge 5000 series hydraulic presses, with integrated IoT for predictive maintenance, captured significant share here, contributing over 30% of the regional growth. Tariffs on Chinese imports have also played to our advantage, with U.S. customers prioritizing North American-sourced equipment to mitigate supply chain risks. FX was a modest tailwind, adding about 1 point to growth.

Shifting to Europe, which represented 24% of revenue at $307 million, growth moderated to 12% year-over-year but was flat sequentially. Headwinds from elevated energy costs—still 20-30% above pre-Ukraine levels—and softening industrial production PMI readings in Germany and Italy weighed on volumes. That said, our focus on energy-efficient equipment resonated strongly; sales of our EcoLink modular assembly lines, compliant with the EU Green Deal's Scope 3 emissions targets, grew 35% year-over-year in the region. Key wins include a €150 million multi-year contract with Siemens for wind turbine gearbox manufacturing in Denmark and expansions with Airbus suppliers in France. We're navigating FX headwinds from a stronger euro, which shaved 2 points off reported growth, but our localized production in our Czech Republic facility—now at 85% capacity utilization—has helped preserve margins at 28% regionally.

Asia-Pacific delivered 25% of total revenue, or $320 million, with 15% year-over-year growth and 4% sequential improvement. China remained the linchpin at 60% of APAC revenue, though growth there decelerated to 10% year-over-year amid property sector deleveraging and slower EV adoption post-subsidy cuts. Positively, our Fanuc-compatible robotic palletizers saw outsized demand from semiconductor fabs in Shanghai, supporting clients like SMIC amid U.S. export controls. India and Southeast Asia were the bright spots, surging 28% year-over-year on infrastructure buildouts—PLIPAC in Indonesia and 'Make in India' incentives driving orders for our high-precision lathes. We've invested $50 million in a new Bengaluru assembly plant to serve this market, reducing lead times by 25% and boosting localization to 70%. Geopolitical tensions and yen weakness provided a 3-point FX tailwind.

Finally, Rest of World contributed 4% of revenue, or $51 million, up 8% year-over-year. Latin America, particularly Mexico's nearshoring boom, grew 20% with maquiladora expansions for U.S. auto exporters like GM. Middle East demand ticked up modestly on oil & gas maintenance capex, though we're prioritizing selective exposure to avoid volatility.

In summary, our diversified footprint—45% Americas, 24% Europe, 31% APAC/ROW—de-risked performance amid patchy global PMIs. Strategically, we're accelerating Industry 4.0 integrations, like AI-driven adaptive controls in our next-gen DynoBot welders, which have a 40% higher uptime versus legacy systems. This positions us for mid-teens growth in FY2025, with North America and emerging APAC as key drivers. Margins expanded 220 basis points to 26.5% overall, thanks to pricing discipline and supply chain efficiencies from our SAP S/4HANA rollout.

Turning now to order intake, which continues to underscore the strength of our positioning in the industrial equipment sector amid accelerating capex cycles and secular tailwinds like electrification and smart manufacturing. In the quarter, we delivered total order intake of $1.52 billion, up a robust 18% year-over-year on a reported basis, and 20% organically excluding a modest 2-point foreign exchange headwind. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, reflecting sustained demand for our core portfolio of CNC machining centers, robotic automation systems, and precision forging equipment—products that power everything from EV battery production lines to wind turbine components.

Breaking it down by segment, our Discrete Automation division, which includes our flagship RoboForge series of collaborative robots and high-speed milling machines, led the way with $785 million in orders, surging 25% year-over-year. This was fueled by major wins, including a $150 million follow-on order from a leading North American OEM for lithium-ion cell manufacturing equipment, capitalizing on the EV supply chain reshoring trend. Our book-to-bill ratio here expanded to 1.25x, up from 1.15x a year ago, driving our segment backlog to a record $2.1 billion. Process Equipment, encompassing our heavy-duty hydraulic presses and material handling systems for mining and metals, posted $520 million in intake, up 12% year-over-year. Strength here came from infrastructure-related demand, with notable bookings from Latin American copper miners upgrading to our energy-efficient ElectroForge presses, which reduce power consumption by up to 30% through variable frequency drive integration. Motion and Power Systems—our electric drivetrains and servo motors—saw $215 million, a solid 10% year-over-year increase, bolstered by aerospace aftermarket recovery, including a $75 million multi-year contract with a Tier-1 supplier for hybrid propulsion test rigs.

Regionally for orders, North America contributed 48% of intake at $730 million, up 28% year-over-year, propelled by IIJA funding into data centers and semiconductor fabs like TSMC's Arizona expansion. EMEA was 32% at $490 million, growing 15% year-over-year, with green hydrogen and offshore wind projects like Siemens Gamesa's nacelle upgrades. Asia-Pacific, at 17% or $260 million, grew 5% year-over-year despite softer Chinese industrial capex, mitigated by diversification into India with a $50 million automotive stamping order. Latin America added the rest on mining tailwinds. These results validate our 'Forge Forward' initiative, our $250 million multi-year R&D push into Industry 4.0, with AI-driven predictive maintenance across 70% of new designs yielding a 15% win-rate uplift. Our trailing 12-month book-to-bill now stands at 1.18x, with total backlog at $4.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year.

Before we move on, a quick note on outlook for end market growth in the near and medium term. As a leader in precision CNC machining centers, industrial automation systems, and heavy-duty material handling equipment serving semiconductors, automotive OEMs, aerospace, mining, and construction, our visibility comes from our backlog, strong book-to-bill ratios, and dialogues with customers like TSMC, Caterpillar, and Boeing. For the near-term—balance of 2024 through 2025—we expect modest but steady end market growth of 3-5% globally, accelerating to 5-7% by Q4 '25 as capex cycles normalize post-2023 inventory destock. Semiconductors, 12% of revenue, sees robust demand from AI data centers and advanced node fabs, with CHIPS Act funding fueling 8-10% capex growth, led by APAC. Automotive, 18% of mix, benefits from EV gigafactories driving 15% growth in welding robots, with North America leading via IRA incentives. Aerospace & Defense, 22%, in multi-year upcycle with 6-8% growth on airframe backlogs and DoD budgets. Mining, 12%, rides commodity supercycle with copper and lithium prices boosting expansions; construction, 15%, uneven but solid in U.S. infrastructure. North America, 45% of sales, is our growth engine at 5-6% near-term, fueled by reshoring—U.S. manufacturing PMI at 49 but new orders subindex stronger.

Gross margin was 28%, driven by favorable mix and pricing. Operating expenses were controlled, resulting in an operating income reflecting solid expansion. Our net income for the quarter supports strong EPS. We are managing our capital allocation effectively, prioritizing investments in high-growth areas and returning capital to shareholders.

Thank you. Next, I will hand over to David Ramirez, COO, for an operational update.

David Ramirez (COO):
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've been focused on improving productivity and efficiency across our manufacturing facilities. We have implemented lean manufacturing principles and are leveraging data analytics to optimize our processes, achieving capacity utilization rates above 85% in key plants like our Czech Republic and Bengaluru facilities. We are also investing in new technologies to enhance our supply chain resilience, including localized sourcing to counter geopolitical risks and Red Sea disruptions, while our IndustroLean 2.0 program is delivering $45 million in annual savings through SAP S/4HANA efficiencies.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, David. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. Our new ApexEdge 2.0 IIoT platform and SecurePAC cyber-resilient suites are showing promising early results, with impacts including 17% OEE improvements and 24% downtime reductions for clients. Building on digital twins and edge AI partnerships like NVIDIA, we believe these technologies will transform the industrial landscape and create significant opportunities for Global Industrial Dynamics Corp., supporting mid-teens growth and margin expansion.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, John. As Mark touched on earlier, our digital solutions are a core part of our Automation segment's 42% surge, driven by IIoT platforms like ApexEdge delivering real-time optimization and 78% gross margins. Customer ROI is tangible—17% OEE gains, 24% less downtime—and we're scaling with 15,000 nodes shipped, focusing on semiconductors and EVs. This annuity revenue positions us for 25-30% growth through 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

Mark Thompson:
Great question, Maria. Emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia are bright spots, with 28% growth in APAC orders from 'Make in India' and infrastructure. We've invested $50 million in Bengaluru for 70% localization, cutting lead times 25%, and secured wins like Maruti Suzuki stamping lines. Nearshoring in Mexico via ROW up 20% complements this, de-risking via diversification while targeting mid-teens FY2025 growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Wilson (Morgan Stanley):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

David Ramirez:
Thanks, Tom. We're tackling this head-on through workforce development, including upskilling programs in AI and automation at our plants, partnering with community colleges for CNC training. Digital tools like predictive maintenance reduce labor dependency by 15%, and reshoring incentives help attract talent. Capacity at 88-92% gives flexibility without aggressive hiring.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Dynamics Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders. One final note on operating margin guidance to wrap up the financial picture. We delivered 14.2% this quarter, up 110 basis points year-over-year, and for Q4, we're guiding 13.8% to 14.8%, with full-year 2024 raised to 14.3% to 15.1%. This reflects pricing up 2.5-3.2%, gross margins 28.5-29.5%, OpEx leverage from zero-based budgeting, and mix toward high-margin automation and services at 32% of revenue. Tailwinds include productivity savings, backlog conversion, and resilient verticals like construction and aerospace, with risks from inputs or FX managed via hedging. We're positioned to outperform cycles.

Sarah Jenkins (VP of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
